extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and authors preparing to submit preprints to arXiv (registered arXiv authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Platform-specific submission requirements and procedural guidance for depositing articles (preprints) on arXiv, including allowed file formats, metadata, file naming, figure inclusion, versioning, and announcement scheduling. Targets authors preparing and uploading their own submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered submitter requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions only from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only users with an arXiv account may submit. Authors are expected to make their own submissions (third-party submissions are discouraged as they often cause problems).

rubrics_metrics.name: License requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must grant arXiv.org a non-exclusive and irrevocable license to distribute or certify that the work is available under another license that conveys these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At submission authors must choose/confirm licensing so arXiv has the right to distribute the work. Ensure any alternate license conveys equivalent distribution rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted text formats (preferred order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission to the archive must be in one of the following formats (listed in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX; PDF; PostScript; HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ArXiv's goal is to store portable, stable formats. TeX/LaTeX is preferred because it 'does not hide information.' Users of word processors should save as PDF and submit that.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disallowed text/scan formats
rubrics_metrics.description: ArXiv will not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source. Scanned documents are not accepted regardless of format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not upload DVI or PS files, or PDFs that are merely renderings of TeX sources where source submission is expected. Scanned PDFs (e.g., images of pages) are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures can be in common formats: PostScript (PS/EPS) for line drawings/plots, JPEG for photographs, GIF or PNG for non-photographic bitmaps, PDF figures only with PDFLaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the format appropriate for the figure type. PDF figures should only be used when compiling with PDFLaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure size and bandwidth considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: If figure files are too large, readers with poor network connections may not be able to download them; make all possible efforts to reduce size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce file size where possible; include large figures if necessary but optimize. If you have problems with a large submission, contact arXiv administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not omit figures/tables/sections; no 'abstract only' submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: ArXiv does not accept submissions with omitted figures, tables or sections. 'Abstract only' submissions are also not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must be complete and useful to readers; providing only partial content or just an abstract is unacceptable and will be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: ArXiv will accept only the following characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other character (spaces, question marks, asterisks, etc.) will cause the system to reject the file upload or submission. Use only the allowed characters to ensure portability.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name case sensitivity and internal references
rubrics_metrics.description: File names and extensions are case sensitive on our system (e.g., Figure1.PDF and figure1.pdf are not the same). Internal file references such as LaTeX figure inclusion commands must match case exactly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that file names used in LaTeX \\includegraphics or other references exactly match uploaded file names, including case, regardless of whether your local OS is case-insensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of data sets and ancillary files
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limited facilities for including data sets and ancillary files (data, programs, etc.) which are associated with articles submitted to arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the separate instructions about including data sets and ancillary files; be aware of limitations and packaging requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title/Abstract metadata preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate instructions exist on the preparation of title/abstract information; this information is used on the abstract pages, in announcements, in RSS feeds, and to support searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare concise, accurate title and abstract metadata per arXiv guidance to ensure correct display and discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check submission and processed files before finalizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the final 'Submit Article' step, check carefully both the title/abstract (metadata) and the processed files. If you see errors or formatting problems correct them or contact arXiv administrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the processed (rendered) files shown by arXiv to ensure there are no issues. Resolve formatting/compilation errors prior to final submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsubmit and edit policy prior to announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you discover an error after submission but before public announcement then select the Unsubmit icon to return it to incomplete status allowing modification and later resubmission. Edits before an article is publicly announced will not generate additional versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Unsubmit to correct errors without creating an extra version; final submission time determines the date stamp. Edits and final submission before 14:00 US Eastern Time Monday–Friday will not delay announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versioning policy and replacement for corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: We encourage authors to update and to make corrections in their articles. DO NOT make a new submission for a corrected article or for an erratum. Rather replace the original submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace/update the existing submission rather than creating a new separate submission for corrections or errata to keep the record consolidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement timing and availability policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are normally made public on Sunday through Thursday, with no announcements Friday or Saturday. There is a schedule (freeze windows) that maps submission receipt times (all times Eastern US) to announcement times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the daily announcement cutoffs (e.g., submissions received between Monday 14:00 - Tuesday 14:00 are announced Tuesday 20:00, etc.). Check current time and time remaining before the 'freeze' to manage timing of your submission and any edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX figures: use standard macro packages
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit figures with your (La)TeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., the graphics and graphicx packages) so that the figures will appear in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on common, supported packages to ensure arXiv's processing can render your figures correctly. ArXiv administration cannot provide help with TeX-related issues; seek help from colleagues if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author metadata requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional affiliation for the author(s) must be provided. Official report number(s) from the author(s) institution(s) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete institutional metadata and report numbers at submission as these are required fields.
